The invention relates to a method for transferring unit loads (6-1, 6-2) to storage channels (15) for storage, the unit loads being conveyed to the storage channels by means of a unit load receiving device (7) which is movable along the storage channels in an x-direction and by means of a transport device (28) which can be extended into the storage channel in a z-direction. The transport device comprises outer transport elements (64, 65) in opposite end sections and optionally an inner transport element (66) in between. The unit load is moved from the unit load receiving device into the storage channel up to an intermediate position (ZP) by means of one of the transport elements (64, 65, 66) by moving the transport device in a first direction of adjustment (68). The transport device is then moved back to a second direction of adjustment (69) such that the other of the transport elements (64, 65, 66) is positioned behind a side wall (70) of the unit load facing the unit load receiving device. The unit load is finally shifted in the storage channel from the intermediate position (ZP) to the second depth position (Zn+1) by means of the other of the transport elements (64, 65, 66) by moving the transport device.

outputs.L1: The invention relates to a method for transferring unit loads (6-1, 6-2) into storage channels (15) for storage. The unit loads are conveyed to the storage channels by a unit load receiving device (7), which is movable along the storage channels in an x-direction, and by a transport device (28), which is extendable into the storage channel in a z-direction. The transport device comprises outer transport elements (64, 65) arranged in opposite end sections and, optionally, an inner transport element (66) arranged therebetween. By moving the transport device in a first adjustment direction (68), one of the transport elements (64, 65, 66) moves the unit load from the unit load receiving device into the storage channel as far as an intermediate position (ZP). The transport device is then moved back in a second adjustment direction (69) until another of the transport elements (64, 65, 66) is positioned behind a side wall (70) of the unit load facing the unit load receiving device. Finally, by moving the transport device, the other transport element (64, 65, 66) shifts the unit load within the storage channel from the intermediate position (ZP) to the second depth position (Zn+1).
outputs.L2:
The invention concerns a process for placing unit loads (6-1, 6-2) into storage channels (15). A unit-load receiving device (7), movable in the x-direction alongside the channels, conveys the loads to the appropriate channel. A transport device (28), extendable into the channel in the z-direction, then handles insertion. The transport device includes outer transport elements (64, 65) at its opposite ends and may also include an intermediate transport element (66).

By moving the transport device in a first adjustment direction (68), one of the transport elements (64, 65, 66) advances the unit load from the receiving device into the storage channel until it reaches an intermediate position (ZP). The transport device is subsequently returned in a second adjustment direction (69), placing another transport element (64, 65, 66) behind the side wall (70) of the load that faces the unit-load receiving device. Further movement of the transport device causes this other transport element to push the load from the intermediate position (ZP) to a second depth position (Zn+1) within the storage channel.
outputs.L3:
The invention provides a method for transferring unit loads into storage channels by means of a receiving device that is movable along the storage channels in an x-direction. The receiving device includes an extendable transport device configured to move in a z-direction, generally transverse to the x-direction. The transport device comprises outer transport elements arranged at opposite ends and may additionally include at least one inner transport element positioned between the outer transport elements.

During operation, a first transport element engages the unit load and moves it from the receiving device into a selected storage channel. The unit load is initially advanced only as far as an intermediate position within the channel. The transport device then reverses its direction of movement so that another transport element is positioned behind the side wall of the unit load that faces the receiving device. This other transport element subsequently engages the unit load and shifts it from the intermediate position to a second, deeper position within the storage channel. In this way, unit loads can be transferred efficiently to different depth positions using a compact, bidirectionally movable transport device.
outputs.L4:
The invention relates to a system and method for transferring unit loads, such as pallets, containers, or load carriers, into storage channels of a storage installation. The system comprises a receiving device that can be moved along the storage channels and positioned in front of a selected channel. An extendable transport device is arranged on the receiving device and includes a plurality of transport elements that can be displaced and selectively brought into engagement with the unit load.

To place a unit load in a storage channel, the receiving device is first aligned with the selected channel. The transport device then engages the unit load with at least one of its transport elements and advances the load from the receiving device into the channel. During this initial transfer, the unit load is moved to an intermediate position that can be reached by the active transport element.

After the load has reached the intermediate position, the transport elements are repositioned. A further transport element is extended or otherwise moved into engagement with the unit load, while the transport element used for the initial movement is released, retracted, or returned to a starting position. The newly engaged transport element then advances the unit load from the intermediate position to a storage position located deeper within the channel. This sequence may be repeated, where necessary, to reach additional storage positions.

The coordinated use of multiple transport elements increases the effective transfer range of the transport device without requiring a single transport element to extend over the entire depth of the storage channel. The arrangement can therefore be made comparatively compact while still permitting reliable placement of unit loads in deep storage locations. Sequential engagement also enables controlled movement of the load and reduces the space, structural complexity, and drive power that may otherwise be required for long-stroke transfer mechanisms.

The same operating principle may be applied in reverse when retrieving a unit load. In that case, one transport element first moves the load from a deeper storage position to an intermediate position, after which another transport element engages the load and transfers it from the intermediate position onto the receiving device. The receiving device can then travel to another storage channel, a transfer station, or an unloading location.

Accordingly, the invention provides an efficient and flexible solution for storing and retrieving unit loads in channel-based storage systems. By dividing the transfer operation into successive movement stages and selectively repositioning the transport elements between those stages, loads can be moved accurately over relatively large channel depths while maintaining a compact construction of the receiving and transport devices.

**The**

“The” is one of the smallest yet most important words in the English language. Known as the definite article, it points to a specific person, place, object, or idea. We say “the book” when we mean a particular book, or “the sun” because there is only one sun in our everyday experience.

Although it often goes unnoticed, “the” brings clarity and precision to communication. It helps listeners and readers understand exactly what is being discussed. Without it, many sentences would sound incomplete or ambiguous.

This simple word also demonstrates how language depends on small details. “The” may contain only three letters, but it plays a powerful role in shaping meaning.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write an abstract for a patent concerning a storage system with a movable unit-load receiving device and an extendable transport device having multiple transport elements.
counterfactuals.output: A storage system includes a storage structure having a plurality of storage locations, a unit-load receiving device movable relative to the storage structure, and an extendable transport device carried by the unit-load receiving device. The transport device includes a plurality of transport elements arranged for movement relative to one another between a retracted configuration and at least one extended configuration. The transport elements cooperate to transfer a unit load between the unit-load receiving device and a selected storage location. A drive mechanism selectively extends and retracts the transport elements and actuates a load-engaging member to support, push, pull, or otherwise convey the unit load. The transport elements may be extended in opposite directions to service storage locations on different sides of the unit-load receiving device. A controller coordinates movement of the receiving device and the transport device to store and retrieve unit loads while reducing transfer space and improving access to storage locations.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Based on the patent specification, describe the method for moving unit loads (6-1, 6-2) from a receiving device (7) into a second depth position (Zn+1) within a storage channel (15).
counterfactuals.output:
The receiving device (7) is aligned with the entrance of the selected storage channel (15). The unit loads are then introduced sequentially:

1. The leading unit load (6‑1) is transferred from the receiving device into the channel to the first depth position \(Z_n\).
2. The following unit load (6‑2) is advanced into the channel.
3. During this continued insertion movement, unit load 6‑2 pushes/displaces unit load 6‑1 by one storage pitch, so that unit load 6‑1 reaches the second, deeper position \(Z_{n+1}\).
4. Unit load 6‑2 remains in the nearer position \(Z_n\).

Thus, the deeper storage position is reached by using the subsequent unit load and the transfer movement from the receiving device to advance the previously inserted load farther into the channel.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Explain, in formal technical language, how the outer transport elements (64, 65) and optional inner transport element (66) cooperate to shift a unit load through an intermediate position (ZP) into storage.
counterfactuals.output:
The outer transport elements (64, 65) are arranged to act on mutually opposite outer regions of the unit load and are driven in a coordinated manner to displace the unit load along the storage direction. They initially receive and support or engage the unit load, then advance it from the transfer region to an intermediate position (ZP), while maintaining its prescribed orientation and lateral alignment.

Where an inner transport element (66) is provided, it extends into or acts within the space between the outer transport elements (64, 65). At the intermediate position (ZP), the unit load enters the effective range of the inner transport element (66). The transport elements are controlled with an overlap in engagement so that the inner transport element assumes the propulsive function before, or substantially as, the outer transport elements release the unit load. The inner transport element then continues the displacement from ZP to the final storage position.

Accordingly, the transport sequence comprises:

1. coordinated engagement of the unit load by the outer transport elements (64, 65);
2. displacement and alignment of the unit load up to the intermediate position (ZP);
3. transfer of the load-driving function to the optional inner transport element (66); and
4. continued advancement by the inner transport element into the storage position.

This staged, overlapping handover provides substantially continuous transport while avoiding uncontrolled movement or loss of alignment at ZP. If the inner transport element (66) is omitted, the outer transport elements remain engaged and perform the displacement through ZP into the storage position.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a concise European-patent-style invention summary for a method of transferring unit loads into storage channels, including the x- and z-direction movements and the first and second adjustment directions (68, 69).
counterfactuals.output: The invention relates to a method for transferring unit loads into storage channels of a storage system. A transfer device carrying a unit load is moved in an x-direction to a selected storage channel and in a z-direction to the level of the selected channel. The position of the unit load relative to the channel is then corrected in a first adjustment direction (68) and a second adjustment direction (69), independently of the x- and z-direction movements, before the unit load is transferred into the storage channel. The additional adjustment movements permit accurate alignment with the channel and reliable load transfer despite positional or dimensional tolerances.
